source.title: Label Denoising through Cross-Model Agreement
source.authors: Yu Wang; Xin Xin; Zai-Qiao Meng; Xiang-Nan He; J. Jose; Fu-Li Feng

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though some figures and flattened tables are not recoverable from the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests a related proposition about agreement across models on clean versus noisy examples and develops denoising from that signal. Its evidence concerns prediction differences and noisy-label classification performance, not whether standard training fits completely random labels or the other specific behaviors in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own clean/noisy prediction-difference results in Figures 1 and 2. The image-classification accuracy table reports DeCA(p) and baselines under random label corruption, but does not measure training error or the claim versions' specific training behaviors, so it is not a row. Other cited claims about memorizing random labels are prior work, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study invokes random-label memorization to motivate denoising, but measures prediction agreement and downstream performance. It reports neither training-label fit nor separate clean/noisy learning trajectories. Table 4 shows declining test accuracy across 10–50% corruption, but does not establish V4's perfect training fit or progression to chance. Figure 3 attributes performance changes to memorization without measuring noisy-label acquisition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report greater agreement on clean examples and improved robustness with DeCA variants in recommendation and image classification. They also acknowledge that DeCA(p) takes twice as long as regular training and can become complex with many classes. Their attribution of performance deterioration to noisy-label memorization is not a direct measurement of that behavior.
record.recipe_differences: This study compares predictions across distinct models and random seeds and proposes a denoising training framework; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and whether predictions are compared across distinct models or across random seeds; the paper reports the qualitative clean/noisy agreement pattern in both recommendation and MNIST settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report greater prediction consistency on clean examples across model pairs and random seeds in MovieLens and MNIST. The MNIST equality-indicator definition conflicts with the disagreement interpretation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean examples receive more consistent predictions across models and seeds than noisy examples in these settings, subject to clarification of the MNIST measure.

record.peer_reviewed: ACM Trans. Recomm. Syst. (publication details in supplied text are volume 0, issue 0)
record.problems: The prediction-difference measurements are shown only in figures, without recoverable exact values or uncertainty. MNIST uses one stated 40% corruption level for the motivation comparison. These experiments do not measure the claim versions' specified behaviors.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results omitted. The image-classification accuracy results in Table 4 compare denoising methods on corrupted-label test accuracy, not training error, fit of random labels, chance test error, or training dynamics; they do not meet the row-to-version criteria.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error with completely random labels under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions. DeCA(p)'s reported twofold training cost compares training methods, not label conditions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout corruption levels and steady degradation from clean labels to fully random labels at chance. Table 4 reports only test accuracy over 10–50% corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization when removed.
Direct comparison of when shared real patterns and noisy labels are acquired during training.

record.verdict_notes: Retain the agreement results as related findings, with no claim-version verdicts. Exact figure values cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The paper's qualitative description establishes its intended agreement finding, but neither agreement nor downstream accuracy establishes random-label training fit or clean-before-noise acquisition.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard deep networks fit completely random training labels with the original architecture and hyperparameters, and their test error.
Training-time cost of fitting random versus true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and test error across corruption levels, including whether test error rises steadily toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation permit fitting random labels or their necessity for true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.
